questions.stem_markdown: A 7-month-old infant has had persistent watering of one eye since early infancy. There is no fever and no sign of local infection. The parents ask when specialist referral is usually needed if this has still not resolved. What is the **best advice**?

options.text: Arrange urgent ophthalmology review now because spontaneous resolution after 6 months is unlikely
Start antibiotics now despite there being no signs of infection
Continue observation for now; if it is still blocked at **12 months**, then refer
Immediate lacrimal probing is the standard next step in primary care
Patch the unaffected eye to reduce the risk of amblyopia

questions.explanation_markdown: The source material supports **observation for nasolacrimal duct obstruction**, with spontaneous resolution expected by about **1 year of age**. Referral is suggested if it remains blocked at that point, and antibiotics are reserved for **signs of infection**.

why_others_wrong.A: The source material does not support routine urgent referral at 7 months in an otherwise uncomplicated case.
why_others_wrong.B: Antibiotics are only indicated when there are signs of infection.
why_others_wrong.D: Immediate probing is not the usual first step described in the uploaded files.
why_others_wrong.E: Patching is not the management approach given for nasolacrimal duct obstruction in the source material.

key_takeaways: Nasolacrimal duct obstruction often resolves spontaneously.
Persistent uncomplicated obstruction is usually observed until about 12 months.
Antibiotics are for superimposed infection, not simple tearing alone.

Fixed splitting of the second heart sound
Normal growth and exercise tolerance
No cyanosis
A murmur heard in an otherwise well child

why_others_wrong.A: A vibratory early systolic murmur is the reassuring innocent-murmur description given in the source material.
why_others_wrong.C: Normal growth and exercise tolerance do not provide the specific discriminator asked for here.
why_others_wrong.D: Lack of cyanosis does not distinguish an innocent murmur from ASD in the uploaded files.
why_others_wrong.E: Being otherwise well is not the examination clue that changes the diagnosis.

key_takeaways: Fixed splitting of the second heart sound is a classic clue for ASD in the source set.
Innocent murmurs are described as vibratory early systolic.
Examination pattern recognition can change whether a murmur is simply observed or investigated.

questions.stem_markdown: A cyanosed newborn undergoes a hyperoxia test. After breathing 100% oxygen, the arterial **PaO2** remains **6.0 kPa**. Which interpretation is **most appropriate**?

options.text: Restricted pulmonary blood flow is likely
This is a reassuringly normal hyperoxia response
This fits no pulmonary restriction with arterial-venous mixing
A primary parenchymal respiratory cause is confirmed
A cardiac cause has effectively been ruled out

questions.explanation_markdown: The uploaded summary states that **very low PaO2 despite 100% oxygen** supports **restricted pulmonary blood flow**. Intermediate responses are used for venous-arterial mixing patterns, whereas a strong rise would argue away from that severe cardiac physiology.

why_others_wrong.B: The source material does not describe a persistently very low PaO2 after 100% oxygen as normal.
why_others_wrong.C: The source distinguishes intermediate responses from the very low range used here.
why_others_wrong.D: The uploaded material instead points to restricted pulmonary blood flow for this degree of non-response.
why_others_wrong.E: The source specifically treats poor hyperoxia response as evidence against ruling out a cardiac problem.

key_takeaways: Hyperoxia testing is about how much PaO2 rises with 100% oxygen.
A very poor rise suggests restricted pulmonary blood flow.
Intermediate responses are interpreted differently from profoundly low ones.

why_others_wrong.E: The source material does not recommend avoiding all live vaccines because of egg allergy.

key_takeaways: Egg allergy does not automatically prevent MMR vaccination.
The source pack supports giving MMR under appropriate supervision.
Parent counselling on contraindications is an important community paediatrics skill.
